articles.title: Jazz Tops PTA Network Quality Survey in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
articles.description: Jazz emerged as the top performer in the PTA's live network quality survey across Islamabad and Rawalpindi on November 5, leading rivals on speed, voice calls and mobile data quality.
articles.sources: TechX, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Jazz topped the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority's latest network quality survey in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, beating every other mobile operator on speed, voice calls and mobile data quality, TechX reported on November 5.

How the survey was run

The PTA ran the live Quality of Experience and Quality of Service field exercise on November 5, 2026, putting all four networks through their paces across the capital's busiest roads. Three dedicated teams ran parallel assessments along routes covering the New Islamabad International Airport, T-Chowk, Murree Road via Faizabad, Rawal Road, the old airport area, Srinagar Highway, Constitution Avenue, Club Road and other connecting corridors. The initial assessment found mobile call and data services generally satisfactory in most inspected areas, but teams also identified shortcomings in call quality and internet services at certain locations. The survey was attended by senior PTA officials including Member (Finance) Muhammad Naveed, Member (Compliance and Enforcement) Dr. Khawar Siddique Khokhar, Member (Telecom) Muhammad Jahanzeb Rahim and Director General (Enforcement) Brigadier (Retd.) Amir Shehzad.

A season of checks

The November 5 exercise was not the regulator's first this season. It followed a shorter network performance survey conducted on Saturday, October 31, by the PTA's Director General (Enforcement), as the regulator continues to monitor improvements following recent network upgrades, optimisation activities and more efficient use of spectrum. The PTA inspected 184 mobile sites from October 22 to 28, 2026, pushing its cumulative count of monitored sites past 900, according to the report.

Jazz's recent record

The result continues a strong run for Jazz in the regulator's rankings. Jazz emerged as Pakistan's best-performing mobile network in the PTA's Independent Quality of Service Survey for the first quarter of 2026, securing the highest overall ranking in 14 of the 18 surveyed cities. In the second quarter, Jazz ranked first in Quetta, Peshawar, Multan, Lahore, Islamabad, Sukkur, Hub, Abbottabad, Faisalabad and Rawalpindi. Jazz currently has around 75 million subscribers in Pakistan. The report noted that the comparative assessment highlighted progress by mobile operators in improving service quality, with Jazz's performance reflecting the combined impact of additional spectrum, network modernisation and accelerated 5G deployment — though voice quality does not always move in the same direction as data performance, and the regulator's checks are continuing.

articles.title: Pakistan and Russia Explore Joint Technology Projects in AI, Cybersecurity and Quantum Computing
articles.description: Pakistan and Russia are exploring commercial partnerships in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and other emerging technologies, with Islamabad seeking to expand digital exports as part of its plan to build a $1 trillion economy by 2035.
articles.sources: Arab News, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan and Russia are exploring commercial partnerships in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and other emerging technologies, with Islamabad seeking to expand digital exports and attract investment as part of its ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2035, officials said on Thursday, Arab News reported on November 5.

The webinar that brought them together

The proposed cooperation was discussed at a Pakistan-Russia technology webinar organised by the Pakistan Software Export Board and Moscow's University of World Civilizations, according to a statement issued by Pakistan's planning ministry. The webinar, the third in a series of bilateral discussions, brought together government officials, industry associations and technology companies from both countries to explore commercial cooperation across different sectors. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said technology had become central to Pakistan's economic transformation, with digital development forming one of the five pillars of the government's URAAN Pakistan economic plan, a national development initiative aimed at accelerating economic growth and expanding exports.

Six priority areas

Discussions between Pakistani and Russian companies covered six priority areas, including artificial intelligence and cloud computing, cybersecurity, digital governance, IT services trade, workforce development and quantum computing. Representatives of Pakistani firms Ebryx and TMC joined Russia's Positive Technologies and Russian Quantum Center in exploring opportunities for joint development and delivery of technology solutions in Pakistan, Russia and third-country markets. Pakistan's IT Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan said the discussions had produced a shortlist of potential projects in cybersecurity, enterprise software, artificial intelligence and cloud computing.

The export backdrop

The government says Pakistan's IT and telecom exports reached a record $4.6 billion in the fiscal year ending June 2026, up around 20 percent from the previous year, as the country seeks to diversify export destinations and move into higher-value digital services. No commercial agreements or investment commitments were announced at the event, the report noted, so the webinar's outcome is best read as an opening — a shortlist of projects and a channel for talks — rather than a signed deal. If the shortlisted projects move forward, they would give Pakistan's software industry a new route into Russian and third-country markets, and give Russian technology firms a partner with a growing export base and a large English-speaking workforce.

articles.title: Pakistan's 5G User Base Reaches 1.8 Million Across 24 Cities — but Lawmakers Question Service Quality
articles.description: Pakistan has about 1.8 million 5G users across 24 cities, the IT minister told a National Assembly committee on Tuesday — up from about 1.3 million in August — while lawmakers questioned why basic 3G and 4G services still struggle.
articles.sources: CW Pakistan, Express Tribune, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan has around 1.8 million 5G users, with services now introduced in 24 cities, Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja told the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecom on Tuesday, CW Pakistan reported on November 4.

The growth figures

Commercial 5G services began in March 2026 after the spectrum auction on March 10. In August, officials had reported about 1.3 million users across 23 cities and more than 1,200 active sites, meaning roughly 500,000 users have been added in under three months, an increase of nearly 38 percent. The number of operational 5G sites has now reached 1,782, according to figures reported after the meeting. PTA Chairman Hafeez ur Rehman also told the committee that 96 million Pakistanis use YouTube, watching around 560 million videos a day, and that Pakistanis make one billion WhatsApp calls daily.

The quality questions

Committee members did not dispute the growth but questioned the quality of networks users already rely on, asking how Pakistan could move towards 5G when users in several areas still struggle with basic 3G and 4G connectivity. One member said mobile internet services had deteriorated since the introduction of 5G, and the committee chairman noted the uneven spread of infrastructure, pointing out that Sukkur, the third largest city in Sindh, has only two 5G sites. The minister acknowledged challenges including infrastructure theft and electricity-related problems affecting tower uptime.

articles.title: Pakistan Weighs Arbitration Over $800 Million in Unpaid PTCL Privatisation Dues
articles.description: Pakistan is considering international arbitration against UAE-based Etisalat, now e&, to recover about $800 million outstanding from the 2005 PTCL privatisation, plus opportunity cost since 2008 and damages, a Senate briefing heard.
articles.sources: Dawn via Profit by Pakistan Today, Thursday Times, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan is considering international arbitration against UAE-based Etisalat, now known as e&, to recover approximately $800 million in outstanding payments from the privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL), along with the opportunity cost since 2008 and applicable damages, Dawn reported via Profit on November 4.

The 20-year dispute

The dispute dates back to 2005, when the government sold a 26 percent stake in PTCL, along with management control, to Etisalat International Pakistan for $2.59 billion. Of that total, $1.76 billion was received, while approximately $800 million remains unpaid. Etisalat tied the balance to the transfer of PTCL properties; of the 3,246 properties covered in the latest briefing, 32 remain untransferred, despite 99 percent having been transferred.

What happens next

The matter was discussed during a joint meeting of the Senate standing committees on information technology and privatisation on Tuesday, where officials said the Office of the Attorney General for Pakistan had been directed to implement the federal cabinet's decision under Rule 24 of the Rules of Business, 1973. In July 2026, a committee headed by the adviser to the prime minister on privatisation recommended considering international arbitration under the sale and purchase agreement. The IT secretary described the matter as sensitive, and the rest of the session was held behind closed doors, reports said.

articles.title: Pakistan Mobile Phone Production Falls 20% in September, but Local Assembly Still Meets 96% of Demand
articles.description: Local manufacturers produced 2.42 million mobile phones in September 2026, down 20% year on year, but up 46% on August — and domestic production met 96% of Pakistan's demand, PTA data showed.
articles.sources: PKRevenue, PTA data, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
Local mobile phone manufacturing and assembly in Pakistan declined by 20 percent year on year in September 2026, despite a strong monthly recovery, according to the latest data released by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), PKRevenue reported on November 3.

The September numbers

Local companies manufactured and assembled 2.42 million units in September 2026, compared with the corresponding period last year, but production increased by 46 percent month on month, indicating an improvement over August. Cumulatively, domestic production declined by 7 percent year on year during the first nine months of 2026, with 21.08 million units produced in January-September 2026 compared with 22.78 million in the same period of 2025. Mobile phone imports declined by 48 percent year on year in September but increased by 38 percent month on month to 110,000 units.

Local assembly still dominates supply

Local manufacturing and assembly met 96 percent of Pakistan's mobile phone demand in September 2026, compared with 95 percent in August. VGO Tel led the locally assembled market during the first nine months of 2026 with production of 2.50 million units, followed by Infinix with 1.96 million and Itel with 1.59 million, PKRevenue reported.

articles.title: Pakistan's First Biomass Energy Plant Becomes Operational in Sajawal, Sindh
articles.description: Pakistan's first biomass energy demonstration plant has become operational in Sajawal, Sindh, under a UNDP-backed project aimed at rural livelihoods, lower emissions and less pressure on forests.
articles.sources: Dawn, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's first biomass energy demonstration plant has become operational in Sajawal, Sindh, to support rural livelihoods, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and ease pressure on forest resources, Dawn reported on November 3.

What the plant is

Located in Pinnah Reserved Forest, the plant was set up under the Global Environment Facility-funded Promotion and Application of Sustainable Biomass Energy Technologies in Pakistan (PASBET) project, implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination. UNDP and the Sindh government jointly inaugurated the plant, the first of four demonstration sites planned under the initiative to showcase scalable woody biomass-based energy technologies.

A five-year, $3.5 million programme

PASBET is a five-year, $3.5 million project that will promote sustainable biomass energy technologies across Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The reports checked did not give the plant's generation capacity or the number of households it will serve, so those figures have not been stated here.

articles.title: AI Demand Lifts Global Trade Outlook to 3.9% — and Opens a Door for Pakistan
articles.description: The WTO has raised its 2026 global merchandise trade growth forecast to 3.9% from 1.9%, citing AI infrastructure investment — with AI-enabling goods driving 47% of the increase in trade value in early 2026.
articles.sources: Wealth Pakistan / Greenpost, WTO October Global Trade Outlook, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure is improving the global trade outlook, with rising demand for semiconductors, servers and other advanced technologies supporting international commerce and creating new opportunities for developing economies, Wealth Pakistan reported from Islamabad on November 2.

The WTO's upgraded forecast

The World Trade Organization has raised its 2026 global merchandise trade volume growth forecast to 3.9 percent from 1.9 percent, citing resilient supply chains and stronger-than-expected investment in AI-related infrastructure. According to the WTO's October Global Trade Outlook and Statistics, AI-enabling goods accounted for 47 percent of the increase in the value of global merchandise trade during the first half of 2026, while trade in these products expanded by 67 percent year over year. The WTO expects AI-related investment to remain an important driver of merchandise trade through 2027.

What it could mean for Pakistan

Muhammad Hafeez, founder and CEO of Nexa Robots Pvt Ltd, told Wealth Pakistan the demand could create opportunities beyond advanced chip manufacturing — in software development, industrial automation, systems integration and technical services. Kazim Ullah, software engineer and co-founder of Devspire Solutions, said the impact extends across sectors, with openings in AI-enabled software, cloud services, data management and technology-enabled business services — practical avenues, he said, for building domestic expertise and expanding technology exports.

articles.title: MUET Students Win Accessibility Award at Alibaba Cloud AI Hackathon Pakistan 2026
articles.description: A Mehran University team won the Special Award in Accessibility at the Alibaba Cloud AI Hackathon Pakistan 2026 national final for Saans, an offline-first app helping frontline workers screen young children for tuberculosis.
articles.sources: CW Pakistan, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Students from the Department of Mechatronics Engineering at Mehran University of Engineering and Technology (MUET), Jamshoro, won the Special Award in Accessibility at the national final of the Alibaba Cloud AI Hackathon Pakistan 2026, held on October 24 in Islamabad, CW Pakistan reported on November 2.

What Saans does

Saans is an English and Urdu, offline-first web application designed to help frontline healthcare workers screen children under five for tuberculosis (TB), using guidelines aligned with those of the World Health Organization. The team received $1,000 and 500 Alibaba Cloud credits for the project. The accessibility award recognises projects that make technology or services easier for people to use — a fitting category for a tool built for frontline workers in low-connectivity settings.

A national showcase

The hackathon was organised by Alkhidmat Foundation's Bano Qabil programme with Alibaba Cloud under the theme 'AI for Pakistan's Future,' with teams from several universities placing in the national final. FAST-NUCES teams took the Grand Champion title and several track awards, while MUET's win came through the special award. The announcement does not say whether the team plans to pilot Saans with health authorities in Sindh or elsewhere, so the next steps for the project are not yet known.

articles.title: 1.5 Million Pakistani Children Faced Online Sexual Exploitation in a Year, UNICEF-Backed Study Finds
articles.description: Nearly one in 16 internet-using children aged 12 to 17 in Pakistan experienced at least one form of technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse in a single year, according to the Disrupting Harm in Pakistan study.
articles.sources: Dawn, IANS via MENAFN, UNICEF / ECPAT International / INTERPOL, Disrupting Harm in Pakistan (September 2026), October 31 - November 1, 2026
articles.body:
About 1.5 million internet-using children in Pakistan experienced sexual exploitation or abuse facilitated by digital technology in a single year, according to new research highlighted in coverage on October 31 and November 1, Dawn and IANS reported.

What the study found

The findings come from Disrupting Harm in Pakistan, a study published in September 2026 by the UNICEF Office of Strategy and Evidence (Innocenti), ECPAT International and INTERPOL, based on a nationally representative household survey of children aged 12 to 17 and their parents or caregivers, plus interviews with frontline and justice professionals. Nearly one in 16 internet-using children in that age group — roughly 1.5 million — experienced at least one form of technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse over 12 months. The reported forms included unwanted sexual images or conversations, demands for intimate photographs, non-consensual sharing of children's images, and sexual threats or blackmail, with AI-generated material flagged as an emerging risk.

Most cases went unreported, the study says

In 85% of the incidents children described, the perpetrator was someone they already knew, challenging the assumption that online abuse mainly comes from strangers, and social media was the most commonly reported setting, accounting for 44% of reported instances. More than half of affected children did not tell anyone, and none of those surveyed reported their experience through formal channels such as a helpline, social worker or police, according to summaries of the study. It also identified gaps in Pakistan's legal and institutional response, including the absence of a systematic requirement for child forensic interviews to be conducted by specially trained professionals, and the continued use of the term 'child pornography' in the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act to refer to child sexual abuse material. Reports note the federal government is considering measures to restrict children's social media use, including a possible minimum age, but no final decision was reported in the cited coverage.

articles.title: Pakistan, OIC and D-8 Explore New Science, Technology and Research Cooperation
articles.description: Pakistan, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and the D-8 explored new cooperation in science, technology, research and innovation at a meeting at the COMSTECH Secretariat in Islamabad on November 1.
articles.sources: Sub News, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Senior diplomat and former Pakistan ambassador to Nepal Abrar H. Hashmi has highlighted new opportunities for cooperation in science, technology, research and innovation among member countries of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the D-8 Organization, Sub News reported on November 1.

A meeting at COMSTECH

Hashmi said he had an excellent interaction with COMSTECH Coordinator General Prof. Dr. Muhammad Iqbal Ch., his team and visiting delegates at the COMSTECH Secretariat in Islamabad. The discussions focused on building on COMSTECH's contributions to advancing science and technology across OIC member states and exploring new avenues of collaboration under a recently signed Memorandum of Understanding with the D-8 Organization.

A network of 31 universities

A key area of discussion was expanding the hosting and activities of the Network of Pioneer Research and Innovation, which connects 31 universities from OIC and D-8 member countries. The network covers research fields including health, energy, agriculture, environment and minerals. The meeting also explored exchanges between centres of excellence and mutual learning, particularly in emerging research areas such as nanotechnology and stem cell research, as reported.

articles.title: Pakistan's Cyber Emergency Team Warns of Spyware That Can Infect Phones Through Online Ads
articles.description: The National Cyber Emergency Response Team has warned that sophisticated spyware can exploit online advertising to steal private data and monitor smartphones without the user clicking a single link.
articles.sources: Daily Pakistan, Citizen Lab research cited by National CERT, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's National Cyber Emergency Response Team has sounded the alarm over a sophisticated spyware threat that can exploit online advertisements to steal private data and secretly monitor smartphones, Daily Pakistan reported on October 31.

What is 'Adfection'?

At the centre of the warning is a cyberattack technique known as Adfection, which turns digital advertising infrastructure into a potential delivery channel for surveillance software. An apparently harmless advertisement appearing on a smartphone could become a gateway for spyware, allowing attackers to access private conversations, pictures, passwords and other sensitive information without the user clicking a single link. The warning raises particular concern for journalists, government officials, researchers and business professionals who handle confidential information on their phones.

What the research found

The advisory follows findings published on October 15, 2026, by Citizen Lab, a research organisation known for investigating digital surveillance. According to the research cited in the advisory, Pakistan was among the countries targeted through an advertising-based spyware campaign, and the investigation identified evidence suggesting certain devices associated with Al Jazeera had been targeted and compromised using Candiru spyware through the same technique. National CERT emphasised that the appearance of an advertisement alone does not confirm that a device has been compromised — the warning is about the technique and the risk, not a claim that every phone showing ads is infected.

articles.title: Pakistan Climbs to 95th in Global Innovation Index 2026, Regaining 'Overperformer' Status
articles.description: Pakistan rose to 95th in the Global Innovation Index 2026 among 139 economies, ranking 72nd on innovation outputs despite sitting 121st on inputs, The Express Tribune noted in an October 31 editorial.
articles.sources: Express Tribune editorial, Global Innovation Index 2026 (WIPO), October 31, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's position in a recent ranking of innovation outputs is a quiet but telling illustration of the country's potential, The Express Tribune said in an editorial on October 31: the country rose to 95th in the Global Innovation Index 2026, regaining 'overperformer' status in the World Intellectual Property Organisation's ranking of 139 economies.

Outputs ahead of inputs

Pakistan ranked 121st on innovation inputs but 72nd on outputs — a gap that suggests the country produces more innovation than its investment levels would predict. The country ranks 10th globally in mobile-app creation relative to GDP, 15th in ICT services exports and 19th in high-tech imports, according to the editorial's reading of the index.

The other side of the ranking

The same index places Pakistan near the bottom on human capital, research and infrastructure. Research and development spending is just 0.16% of GDP, patent filings lag badly, and startup funding — already modest by international standards — has crashed, the editorial noted. The lesson it draws is that the talent and output are there; what is missing is the investment in research, skills and infrastructure to sustain them.

articles.title: Pakistan Launches New E-Passport With Chip, NFC and Biometric Security
articles.description: Pakistan has introduced a new e-passport featuring an electronic chip, NFC technology and laser engraving, with issuance having begun on October 23, 2026, according to the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports.
articles.sources: ProPakistani and Directorate General of Immigration and Passports, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan has introduced a new e-passport featuring advanced chip technology, biometric security and faster identity verification, according to the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports. The new passport began issuing on October 23, 2026, and is designed to bring Pakistan's travel documentation in line with modern international standards.

What is inside the new passport

According to the directorate, the e-passport incorporates a modern electronic chip and Near Field Communication (NFC) technology to improve the protection of personal and biometric information. The document also features laser engraving and an updated design intended to strengthen security and make passports harder to forge.

Why it matters for travellers

The introduction of the e-passport is expected to facilitate faster identity verification and streamline immigration procedures at airports and border crossings. The directorate says the passport incorporates data encryption in line with standards set by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), measures intended to improve the security and reliability of Pakistan's travel documents.

A wider digital identity push

The e-passport rollout fits a broader shift towards chip-based, machine-readable travel documents worldwide, where border systems increasingly read biometric data directly from the document rather than relying on paper-based checks. For Pakistani travellers, the change promises smoother processing at international checkpoints as more countries adopt compatible e-passport readers.

Applicants should check the directorate's official channels for the application process and any updated fee schedule for the new document.

articles.title: Pakistan Targets 50% Local Value Addition in Mobile Phone Manufacturing
articles.description: Pakistan is formulating a new Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy to lift domestic value addition from 10–20% to as much as 50%, after locally producing 20.08 million handsets in the first nine months of 2026.
articles.sources: TechJuice, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan is aggressively pushing to transform its local mobile phone manufacturing sector, with the government formulating a new Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy to shift the industry from import-dependent assembly towards robust local component manufacturing. The Ministry of Industries and Production aims to achieve up to 50% domestic value addition over time, according to reports published on October 30, 2026.

From assembly to components

The upcoming policy builds upon the previous Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy 2020–2023. Its focus is heavily on local component production, technology transfer and the development of a supporting industrial ecosystem. Currently, domestic value addition in mobile device manufacturing hovers around just 10% to 20%, leaving considerable room for growth if local suppliers can scale up.

The scale of local production

Between January and September 2026, Pakistan produced 20.08 million handsets locally, against commercial imports of only 2.85 million units in the same period. The locally assembled devices included roughly eight million smartphones and 12 million 2G phones. Data from the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority shows smartphones now account for 71% of all active mobile devices on local networks. VGO TEL emerged as the largest producer in the nine-month period, with 2.50 million handsets.

Imports are already falling

During the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, the mobile phone import bill fell 16.6% in dollar terms to $417.24 million, from approximately $500.01 million in the same period last year. Imports rose 7.1% month-on-month in September 2026 but remained 28.2% lower year-on-year compared with September 2025, suggesting the local industry is steadily displacing imports.

If the new policy delivers on component localisation, Pakistan's phone industry could move from assembling imported kits to building a deeper domestic supply chain — and keep more of each phone's value at home.

articles.title: PTA Fines Mobile and Internet Firms Over Rs3.41 Billion Over Consumer Complaints
articles.description: Pakistan's telecom regulator has reportedly fined mobile and internet companies over Rs3.41 billion over consumer complaints, while ordering network expansion to improve service quality.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's telecom regulator has reportedly imposed fines of more than Rs3.41 billion on mobile phone companies and internet service providers over consumer complaints, according to reports published on October 29, 2026. The action forms part of continued enforcement against poor service quality, the reports said.

Expansion ordered alongside the fines

Each company has reportedly been instructed to install 1,000 new sites annually to improve network coverage and service quality. An additional 480 MHz of spectrum has also been made available, a move aimed at increasing 4G internet speeds from 14 Mbps to 120 Mbps and enabling speeds of up to 150 Mbps on 5G networks.

Why so many sites are offline

Telecom operators continue to face major operational challenges, with approximately 9,000 mobile sites, accounting for about 17 per cent of the country's total, reportedly remaining non-operational due to electricity load-shedding, right-of-way disputes, power theft and equipment theft from telecom towers. The situation is reported to be particularly concerning in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Gilgit-Baltistan, where network infrastructure faces persistent disruptions. The relevant record has also been presented in the National Assembly.

What the regulator says

A PTA spokesperson said the authority was continuing to take action against mobile phone companies and internet service providers in accordance with the law. The spokesperson added that notices and quality-of-service surveys were being used to address poor performance and ensure uninterrupted services for consumers.

For users, the combination of fines and rollout obligations signals a push to pair penalties with physical network improvement, rather than enforcement alone.

articles.title: PTA Warns of Rising 5G Security Risks as Cyber Alerts Top 10,000
articles.description: PTA's annual security report records over 10,000 cyber alerts and 1,500 escalations, warning that 5G networks face growing threats from data theft to denial-of-service attacks.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's telecom regulator has warned of mounting cybersecurity risks facing the country's 5G networks, according to its latest annual security report covered on October 29, 2026. The report records more than 10,000 cyber alerts, with 1,500 incidents escalated and 534 malicious addresses blocked.

Where the risks sit

According to the findings, vulnerabilities span 5G user devices, radio access networks, core functions, application programming interfaces and cloud-hosted environments. The 5G core remains a primary target because it processes sensitive subscriber records, session management data and routing information, while edge networks face heightened risks due to distributed architectures and containerised workloads. Reported risks range from subscriber data theft and real-time location tracking to devastating denial-of-service attacks.

A tougher rulebook

To address emerging threats, the PTA developed the Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025, revising the framework introduced in 2020. The updated framework expands cybersecurity requirements covering asset management, risk assessment, data privacy, cloud security, insider threats, business continuity and incident response. It also strengthens requirements for identity verification, access controls and coordination with the national telecom security monitoring system.

What operators must do next

The regulator has introduced comprehensive 5G security guidelines emphasising proactive safeguards over retroactive fixes. Operators must implement zero-trust architectures, secure boot mechanisms and AI-driven anomaly detection, with mandatory deployment of advanced identifiers to shield permanent subscriber credentials from interception over the air. Under its proposed 2025-26 audit programme, the regulator plans to require full audit coverage of Category I and Category II telecom licensees and conduct validation audits of selected operators in other categories.

The report emphasised that improving cybersecurity monitoring, strengthening technical controls and expanding cooperation between regulators and telecom operators would be necessary to protect Pakistan's growing digital infrastructure.

articles.title: Pakistan Internet May Slow Until November 2 as AAE-1 Cable Undergoes Repairs
articles.description: PTCL says emergency repairs on the AAE-1 submarine cable between Italy and France may slow internet speeds in Pakistan during peak hours until November 2.
articles.sources: TechJuice, Profit/Pakistan Today, Daily Pakistan, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
Internet users across Pakistan may face slower speeds during peak hours until November 2, 2026, as emergency repairs continue on a major international submarine cable. The Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) said work is being carried out on the AAE-1 (Asia-Africa-Europe 1) cable, specifically on the section between Italy and France.

Why Europe-hosted sites will feel it most

Because the affected segment lies in Europe, users are most likely to experience slower loading times when accessing websites and services hosted in European countries, particularly during evening peak hours. PTCL said repairs have already started and that users may notice minor service degradation, mainly during busy hours, appealing to customers for patience while the work is under way.

The AAE-1 is one of the most important routes for Pakistan's international internet traffic. Stretching about 25,000 kilometres, it links Southeast Asia to Europe via Egypt and lands in Karachi; PTCL began its Pakistani operations on the cable in 2017. The cable has caused disruption before: in January 2025, a fault near Qatar slowed internet speeds nationwide for nearly two weeks. PTCL has not yet said whether additional backup bandwidth will be provided during the current repairs, and the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority had not responded to requests for comment when the story was filed.

articles.title: PM Sets November Deadline for Alibaba-Backed AI and Digitalisation Projects
articles.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed ministries to complete all groundwork by November on AI, digital government, health and agriculture projects being pursued with Alibaba.
articles.sources: APP via TezKhabar, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday directed relevant ministries to complete by November all necessary measures for projects being undertaken with Alibaba to advance artificial intelligence, digitalisation, exports and public service delivery. He issued the directives while chairing a review meeting in Islamabad on progress in AI, digitalisation and cooperation with Alibaba in Pakistan's economy and governance sectors.

What the projects cover

The push spans artificial intelligence, digital government, exports, agriculture, health and the fuel supply chain. The cooperation was sealed during the prime minister's visit to China, when a memorandum of understanding was signed at Alibaba's headquarters in Hangzhou. The prime minister said AI and digitalisation were central to national development, and that the government wants the full benefit of its strategic partnership with Alibaba.

Specific directions included implementing an early cancer detection system with Alibaba's cooperation, launching an AI training programme for IT graduates under the Ministry of Information Technology's Ignite programme, and asking the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority to introduce an analytics system with Alibaba to monitor the petroleum products supply chain. The Export Promotion Board was instructed to work with Alibaba to increase Pakistan's exports, and the prime minister welcomed Alibaba's cooperation in helping Pakistani agricultural commodities reach Chinese markets. The November deadline turns a set of agreements into a delivery timetable, and ministries now have days, not months, to show progress.

articles.title: Pakistan's 5G Now Reaches 24 Cities After $509 Million Spectrum Auction
articles.description: Pakistan has rolled out 5G services at more than 1,700 sites across 24 major cities following its largest-ever spectrum auction, the IT minister told a global digital summit in Seoul.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, October 21, 2026; Mettis Global News, October 20, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan has significantly expanded its digital infrastructure through a major spectrum auction, 5G deployment and nationwide fibre-optic connectivity, Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja told a high-level panel at the Global Digital and AI Summit in Seoul. She said Pakistan viewed artificial intelligence primarily as a network challenge under the Digital Nation Pakistan vision.

Pakistan conducted its largest-ever spectrum auction in March 2026, acquiring 480 MHz of spectrum for $509 million and increasing telecom operators' combined holdings from 274 MHz to 754 MHz. Within six months, 5G services had been launched at more than 1,700 sites across 24 major cities, delivering average speeds of 130 Mbps, the minister said.

Fibre, speeds and international links

Download speeds in the country had risen by 68.1 percent over two years, while more than 234,000 kilometres of optical fibre cable had been deployed nationwide, according to the minister. The government had abolished right-of-way charges to reduce costs and accelerate fibre expansion.

Pakistan is connected to international networks through six submarine cables with combined capacity exceeding 17 terabits per second, and the country is developing the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Digital Corridor to connect Central Asia with the wider world.

Satellite and the road ahead

Highlighting connectivity in remote areas, the minister said regulators were finalising a framework for satellite communications and licensing to facilitate direct-to-device services, with satellite technology complementing rather than replacing terrestrial networks. New frameworks for mobile virtual network operators and infrastructure sharing had also been introduced to attract investment.

With telecom subscribers reported to have crossed 200 million and around 70 percent of the population under the age of 30, the minister said demand for quality digital services would keep rising, making reliable and accessible connectivity central to Pakistan's digital transformation.

The rollout matters beyond headline speeds: reliable, high-capacity networks are the foundation on which artificial intelligence services, remote work, digital payments and online learning all depend. Officials have framed the expansion as part of a wider effort to close connectivity gaps, including in remote areas where satellite services are expected to complement terrestrial networks in the years ahead.

articles.title: Pakistan Announces Urdu AI Model 'Buraq' to Keep National Data at Home
articles.description: Pakistan has announced Buraq, a government-backed Urdu AI model unveiled at a summit in Seoul, designed to understand and generate text in Urdu and other regional languages while keeping Pakistani data inside the country.
articles.sources: TechJuice, October 2026; The Express Tribune, October 21, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's IT minister has announced Buraq, a government-backed Urdu AI model, at a summit in Seoul on October 22. According to Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja, the model will keep all Pakistani data inside the country, addressing concerns about data sovereignty as artificial intelligence tools spread.

Buraq will understand and generate text in Urdu and other regional languages. The decision to build the model from scratch follows a striking gap in global AI training data: Urdu makes up just 0.03 percent of global web content gathered by Common Crawl, which means most existing AI models struggle with the language, TechJuice reported.

Sovereign computing and $1 billion commitment

To support Buraq, Pakistan plans to set up sovereign computing power so that data processing stays within the country. The government has committed $1 billion in funding through 2030 for AI, regulatory changes and public-sector AI projects, including AI deployments in welfare, healthcare and tax systems. The country recently launched its first local AI cloud through a partnership between Telenor Pakistan and Data Vault Pakistan.

The minister also highlighted four digital foundations that Buraq will build on: NADRA's digital identity system, which serves over 100 million Pakistanis; the State Bank's Raast instant payment platform; and the national data exchange WASL, which handles secure data sharing between government agencies.

Human oversight at the centre

Khawaja stressed that AI should help people make decisions, not make decisions for them, and said the government will keep human oversight at the centre of all AI systems. Pakistan's National Data Governance Policy sets rules for storing, sharing and protecting government data. The minister also noted that Pakistan became the first country to sign the Digital and AI Compact at the Seoul summit, describing AI as the last layer, not the first, of digital development.

articles.title: PM Launches Two-Year Drive to Give 500,000 Chromebooks to Talented Students
articles.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on October 25 launched a programme to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks and internet facilities to talented students from schools and seminaries over two years.
articles.sources: Pakistan Today, October 26, 2026.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday launched a programme to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks and provide internet facilities to talented students from schools and religious seminaries across Pakistan over the next two years. Addressing a ceremony organised under the Prime Minister's Youth Programme, he said access to technology and education must not be determined by wealth or poverty.

Merit as the only criterion

The prime minister said intelligence and hard work should not be held captive by wealth and poverty, and that merit and effort should determine which students receive the devices. The selected students are also being provided with bags and MiFi devices to enable them to access the internet, attend classes remotely and use electronic libraries from home. Addressing the students directly, he said that through the Chromebooks they would be able to acquire knowledge and, as they grow up, become some of the most distinguished and capable people in the country.

Building on an earlier laptop programme

Recalling the laptop distribution programme launched under former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, Shehbaz Sharif said 600,000 laptops had been distributed on merit among students across Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The new Chromebook drive is presented as a continuation of that approach, updated for a classroom era in which much learning, revision and research happens online rather than on paper alone.

Wider education push

The prime minister also said 27 Daanish schools are under construction as the government expands access to quality education and digital learning. The Daanish school network, aimed at talented children from disadvantaged backgrounds, has long been part of the Sharif family's education pitch, and pairing new schools with devices and connectivity fits that strategy. The government, he said, was determined to ensure that talented children are not left behind in an increasingly technology-driven world.

What will decide success

The real test of the scheme will not be the launch ceremony but the delivery that follows: whether devices reach the students selected on merit, whether internet access works reliably outside major cities, and whether teachers are supported to use the devices for learning rather than leaving them as prestige objects. Two years is a long window, and the programme's credibility will rest on transparent selection lists and steady distribution. If it works, half a million students will gain a direct route into digital classrooms, online libraries and remote learning that many of their peers already take for granted.

articles.title: Pakistan to Host UN Space Technology Conference on Early Warnings and Climate Action
articles.description: Pakistan's space agency SUPARCO will host a five-day UN conference in Islamabad from October 27 to 31 on using space technology for early warnings, climate action and disaster risk assessment.
articles.sources: The News, October 2026; Pakistan Today, October 22, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan is set to host a five-day international conference in Islamabad from October 27 to 31 on how space technology can strengthen early warning systems, improve disaster risk assessment and support climate action. The event is being organised by the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, known as SUPARCO, and is co-sponsored by the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs through its UN-SPIDER programme, the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization and the Inter-Islamic Network on Space Sciences and Technology.

Who will attend

Organisers expect an estimated 200 to 250 participants, including 60 to 70 international delegates and around 150 national participants. The audience will span experts, policymakers, diplomats, educators, researchers, United Nations agencies, development organisations and representatives of the space industry. The conference will take place at a hotel in Islamabad, with the Serena Hotel named in reports as the venue. That mix matters: early warning systems only work when satellite data, government agencies and local communities are connected, and the conference is designed as a meeting point for all three.

The Early Warnings for All focus

A central focus will be the United Nations' Early Warnings for All initiative, which seeks to protect communities and critical infrastructure against climate-induced disaster events through effective early warning systems. Discussions will explore the role of space technologies in disaster risk reduction, climate-resilient development and the monitoring of water resources, agriculture, forests and environmental change. For Pakistan, a country repeatedly hit by floods, heatwaves and glacial hazards, those topics are not abstract. Satellite observations and geospatial data can track river levels, rainfall, crop stress and forest loss in near real time, giving authorities hours or days of extra warning that can save lives.

Why it matters for Pakistan

Hosting the conference also signals Pakistan's ambition to be taken seriously as a space and climate actor, not just a victim of climate disasters. SUPARCO's work on remote sensing already feeds into agriculture, water management and disaster planning, and an international gathering gives Pakistani researchers a platform to share findings and build partnerships. The test, as with many conferences, will be what survives after the closing session: joint projects, data-sharing agreements and practical tools that district officials can actually use when the next flood warning arrives.

What to watch this week

Over the five days, watch for announcements on training, data access and regional cooperation, as well as any concrete commitments on early warning coverage for vulnerable districts. The conference runs until October 31, and its sessions on water, agriculture and forests are likely to be the most directly relevant to farming communities and provincial disaster agencies across Pakistan.

articles.title: PAK-US Tech Connect 2026 Takes 16 Pakistani Tech Firms Across America
articles.description: Led by the Pakistan Software Export Board, the roadshow visited Silicon Valley, Dallas, Washington DC and Chicago in October, with two startups alongside the established firms.
articles.sources: TechJuice; NetMag Pakistan; The Nation, October 25, 2026.
articles.body:
Through Pak-US Tech Connect 2026, Pakistan is bringing a cohort of top-tier companies known for strong security, clear governance, proven AI capabilities and measurable business impact to the United States. Led by the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB), the multi-city roadshow included engagements in Silicon Valley on October 16, Dallas on October 19, Washington, D.C., on October 21, and Chicago on October 23, 2026.

Who went, and what they sell

The 16 participating companies are Systems Limited, 10Pearls, NETSOL Technologies, IBEX Global Solutions, Techlogix Pakistan, Arbisoft, Folio3 Software, CureMD Healthcare, Tkxel, Strategic Systems International (SSI), Emumba, Abacus, TMC, Nextbridge, Excellence Delivered (ExD), and Addo AI. The delegation comprises Pakistani technology leaders with expertise in artificial intelligence, enterprise software, cloud computing, fintech, cybersecurity, healthcare technology, data engineering and customer experience management. Alongside them, two emerging startups, Swich and Heyeve.ai, represent Pakistan's startup ecosystem. Swich is a fintech with an innovative Web3 merchant financial operating system, while Heyeve.ai focuses on immersive, AI-powered legal training.

Why the United States matters so much

The roadshow reflects Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif's vision of a deeper economic partnership with the United States by facilitating direct business-to-business engagement between Pakistani technology companies and CIOs, CTOs and other senior decision-makers at Fortune 1000 enterprises. The United States is an important destination for Pakistan's technology industry: PSEB officials have said the US accounts for more than half of Pakistan's annual technology exports, making it a significant market for software development and IT-enabled services. In Dallas, Pakistan's Ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, told the gathering that close ties between Pakistan and the US in the technology sector are a necessity rather than a choice, noting that the two countries are among the world's five most populous nations and complement each other in IT and other fields.

What success looks like — and what it does not guarantee

The roadshow is intended to help Pakistani businesses establish direct relationships with prospective clients, demonstrate their capabilities and explore long-term commercial partnerships. In Chicago, the closing leg drew a large number of companies from across the American Midwest, with Illinois State Representative Justin Slaughter and State Senator Laura Murphy among the speakers. But participation in business meetings does not automatically translate into new contracts: as of the published reports, organisers had not disclosed the total value of any signed deals, confirmed investment commitments or additional export revenue generated by the initiative. The honest test of Tech Connect 2026 will come in the months ahead, in signed contracts and export figures — not in the applause at the roadshow itself.

articles.title: Pakistan Wins 11 Awards at the ASOCIO Digital and AI Awards 2026
articles.description: From digital government to AI in cybersecurity, healthcare and finance, Pakistani organisations swept 11 categories at the Jakarta ceremony on October 6.
articles.sources: ProPakistani; Business Recorder; The News, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's digital and artificial intelligence (AI) industry has achieved a significant milestone after securing 11 awards at the ASOCIO Digital and AI Awards 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. The recognition highlights the country's growing capabilities in technology, digital transformation and AI-driven innovation across multiple industries. Organised by the Asian-Oceanian Computing Industry Organisation (ASOCIO), the awards ceremony took place on October 6, bringing together technology organisations from 26 economies across the Asia-Oceania region.

The winners, category by category

Pakistani organisations received recognition in diverse categories, including digital government, talent development, global business services, cybersecurity, education, healthcare, agriculture, financial services, workforce development and manufacturing. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Information Technology Board (KPITB) won the Digital Government Award, while REMIRE received the Talent Development Award and Symmetry Group Limited secured the Global Business Service Award. In the AI categories, SecureBeans was recognised for AI in Cybersecurity, PlanetBeyond Pakistan for AI for Public Good, the Center for Advanced Research in Engineering (CARE) for AI in Education, and DxVision AI for AI in Healthcare. Sybrid Private Limited won the AI in Smart Agriculture Award, while Unikrew Solutions (Private) Limited received the AI in Financial Services Award. Geekinn (Private) Limited was recognised for AI in Workforce and Future Skills, and SMART IS (Private) Limited won the AI in Manufacturing and Supply Chain Award.

What the breadth of the wins signals

The Pakistan Software Houses Association for IT and ITES (P@SHA) welcomed the achievement, with Chairman Dr Shoab A. Khan describing it as an important milestone for Pakistan's IT sector. The breadth matters as much as the count: the wins span public services, classrooms, hospitals, farms, banks, factories and the workforce itself, suggesting applied AI work rather than a single showcase project. A P@SHA delegation attended the event, comprising Chairman Dr Shoab A. Khan, Vice Chairman of ASOCIO and P@SHA Central Executive Committee member Muhammad Zohaib Khan, and Zain Tariq, Head of Special Projects at P@SHA. During the ceremony, the awards for Symmetry Group, SecureBeans and Geekinn were received on behalf of the organisations by members of the delegation.

From awards to exports

Awards do not by themselves create export revenue, but they do change how foreign buyers see Pakistani firms — and that reputational shift is exactly what programmes like Pak-US Tech Connect 2026 are built to convert into contracts. The challenge now is for the winning organisations, from provincial digital government to AI healthcare startups, to turn Jakarta's recognition into pilots, partnerships and paying clients abroad. If they do, October 2026 may be remembered as the month Pakistan's AI story moved from promise to proof.

articles.title: Pakistan Showcases AI Innovations at Abu Dhabi's AI Everything Global 2026
articles.description: Five Pakistani companies presented AI data intelligence, surveillance, sales and sovereign AI solutions at the PSEB pavilion, as IT exports to the UAE hit $536 million.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, October 7, 2026; Geo News; ARY News.
articles.body:
Pakistan is showcasing its growing capabilities in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies at AI Everything Global 2026, one of the region's leading public-private gatherings on AI, bringing together more than 500 exhibitors and 150 investors from 70 countries in Abu Dhabi. Pakistan has established a strong presence at the event, featuring five leading Pakistani technology companies presenting innovative AI-driven solutions and services.

What Pakistan put on show

The five companies are presenting solutions in areas including AI data intelligence, AI surveillance, AI sales solutions and sovereign AI. The pavilion has been established under the Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB), with Pakistan's participation facilitated by the Commercial Section of the Pakistan Diplomatic Mission in the UAE, led by Trade and Investment Counsellor Ali Zeb Khan, in coordination with PSEB and the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication. Sovereign AI — systems designed to keep data and control within a defined ownership boundary — is a growing priority for Gulf governments, and its presence on Pakistan's stand signals an ambition to sell into government and enterprise buyers, not just consumer apps.

An ambassador's pitch for talent

The Pakistan pavilion was inaugurated by Shafqat Ali Khan, Pakistan's envoy to the UAE. The ambassador interacted with participating Pakistani companies and highlighted the importance of enabling Pakistan's technology sector to play a proactive role in the rapidly evolving global AI landscape. Ambassador Khan underscored the need to invest in AI talent development, particularly by equipping the younger generation with advanced AI, coding and digital skills. He emphasised that building a future-ready workforce would be critical to enhancing Pakistan's competitiveness and enabling its technology companies to capitalise on emerging opportunities in the global digital economy.

The trade numbers behind the pavilion

Pakistan's IT exports to the UAE rose 42% to $536 million in the 2025-26 financial year from $376 million in 2024-25, according to Pakistani officials. Pakistan is seeking to further expand its technology exports and promote "Made in Pakistan" and "Developed in Pakistan" products in international markets. The two-day exhibition, held in Abu Dhabi on October 6 and 7, brought together companies, startups, investors and technology experts to showcase AI and its applications across different industries. For the five firms on the pavilion, the real measure of the trip will be the partnerships and deals that follow — but the export trend they are riding is already moving in the right direction. For the five firms on the pavilion, the value of the trip lay not only in the exhibition floor but in the investor meetings and partnership conversations that a gathering of more than 500 exhibitors and 150 investors makes possible.
